mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES rebounds from its recent trough, weekday trip chaining into shops and eateries rises with a lag and pushes RETAIL_REC up over the next four weeks. The effect should be visible after labor mobility stabilizes rather than during a single volatile week.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell to -22.7 at t-1w and recovered to -3.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES remaining above its t-1w level for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT stays deeply negative, access friction suppresses discretionary shopping trips and RETAIL_REC falls within one to two weeks. The mechanism fails if transit mobility normalizes without any improvement in retail visits.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -15 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -20.6 at t-1w and -14.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is higher over the next 14 days even though TRANSIT stays below -15 for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A joint rise in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES increases effective urban circulation, which feeds into more retail and recreation visits over the following four weeks. The signal is strongest when both series move up together rather than separately.
evidence_refs: fact:both series were depressed around t-1w/t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next 28 days when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise from their current levels for at least two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in RESIDENTIAL time signals substitution toward staying home, which lowers discretionary retail visits after about one week. The mechanism is rejected if residential time rises but retail mobility also rises.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 10 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was 12.9 at t-1w and 8.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 7 days after RESIDENTIAL exceeds 10 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: An upswing in GROCERY_PHARM lifts errand density and can spill into nearby retail and recreation trips over the next two weeks. The effect should appear when essential-shopping mobility is moving up, not when it is flat or falling.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved from -3.9 at t-3w to 3.1 at t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not higher over the next 14 days despite GROCERY_PHARM increasing for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility remains elevated while retail mobility is still weak, outdoor leisure competes with indoor shopping and RETAIL_REC declines over the next four weeks. The effect requires a persistent parks rebound rather than a one-week spike.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -10 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped to -8.3 at t-1w before easing to -15.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall over the next 28 days when PARKS stays above -10 for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, lower workplace and transit mobility jointly suppress discretionary shopping, so RETAIL_REC falls within four weeks. The mechanism disappears if policy tightening is absent or if only one mobility channel weakens.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain below baseline in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 28 days while both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain suppressed.

mechanism_narrative: A short-run recovery in GROCERY_PHARM together with falling RESIDENTIAL time indicates more out-of-home errand behavior, which translates into higher retail and recreation mobility within two weeks. The claim fails if grocery mobility rises but people continue spending more time at home.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 10 while GROCERY_PHARM is positive
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM was 3.1 at t-1w and RESIDENTIAL was 12.9 at t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days when GROCERY_PHARM remains positive and RESIDENTIAL drops below 10.
